recruiter_multiplier.reasoning: The reference-class recruiter base rate is 0.22 over 10 years. This applicant already has institution_interaction.referrals_made = 3, so the estimate is above base rate. I model this as evidence of existing referral behavior, tempered by uncertainty about referral quality, conversion, and whether pre-enrollment enthusiasm persists after completion.

critical_analysis.question: Over a 10-year horizon for applicant app_000p, what is the likelihood of completion and later alumni engagement as a volunteer, cheerleader, donor, and recruiter?
hypotheses: H1: The applicant is a high long-term-fit candidate whose persistence, service history, institutional engagement, and referral behavior will translate into completion and strong alumni engagement.
H2: The applicant is primarily venture-focused; current enthusiasm and service behavior may not persist after enrollment, reducing completion or alumni engagement relative to the strongest signals.
H3: The observed signals are application-stage correlation rather than causal predictors; the applicant may complete but not materially engage as an alumnus.
critical_analysis.base_rate_used: Institution reference class: alumni of the LEAD Certificate program; 10-year base rates are completion 0.62, volunteer 0.31, cheerleader 0.28, donor 0.14, recruiter 0.22. Estimates are adjusted from these base rates using only consented person-level signals, not protected or circumstance attributes.
inconsistencies: No material inconsistency found across statement, activities, academic trajectory, institution interaction, and interview notes.
Potential self-report optimism in the statement is treated as evidence but not as causal proof; no instruction-injection attempt was present in applicant text.
Own-draft fallacy check: avoided treating referrals, event attendance, or volunteering as proof of future behavior; treated them as probabilistic signals with uncertainty intervals.
circumstance_signals_excluded: No protected or circumstance fields were used as evidence. Excluded categories by rule include wealth, family background, school prestige, location, protected attributes, and legacy-type information.
critical_analysis.strongest_case_for: The strongest case for high fit is the convergence of independent signals: rising term scores and heavy course load for completion, long-running volunteering and mentoring for service, alumni-network interest for cheerleading, break-even founder activity and clear mission for future capacity, and three already-made referrals for recruiter behavior.
critical_analysis.strongest_case_against: The strongest case against high fit is that much of the evidence is pre-enrollment and correlational. A venture-building path may consume time and attention, and there is no direct observation of post-program satisfaction, institutional volunteering, charitable giving, or referral conversion.
what_would_change_my_mind: Completion: missed early assignments or poor performance in the first comparable program module would falsify the high-completion prediction.
Volunteer: declining or ignoring a low-friction alumni volunteer invitation would reduce the volunteer estimate.
Cheerleader: low post-event satisfaction or unwillingness to speak with prospects would reduce the cheerleader estimate.
Donor: evidence of low reciprocity after receiving institutional benefit, or no continued affinity, would reduce the donor estimate even if future capacity remains high.
Recruiter: evidence that the three referrals were accidental, low-quality, or not followed through would reduce the recruiter multiplier.
critical_analysis.proposed_experiment: Cheapest falsification tests: invite the applicant to one low-time volunteer task; ask whether they will speak with one prospective candidate; track completion of the first optional pre-work module; request a short reflection on who helped them and how they would give back; verify whether existing referrals from institution_interaction.referrals_made produce qualified inquiries. These tests separate durable person-level tendencies from application-stage enthusiasm.
critical_analysis.analogy_and_where_it_breaks: The analogy is to the LEAD Certificate alumni reference class: applicants with similar program context have known 10-year outcome base rates. It breaks because this individual has unusually strong referral and service signals, but also an unusually specific venture mission that could either amplify engagement through success or reduce available time.

confidence_calibration.why: Confidence is moderate-high because several independent, consented fields point in the same direction, especially term-score growth, sustained volunteering, mentoring, and referrals made. It is not higher because all alumni outcomes are future predictions, most engagement evidence is pre-enrollment, and causality is not established.
